current_activity: 1st Battalion landing unopposed at Aola Bay
notes: Miller, ch. VII: the Aola Force included 1,700 men of the 1st Battalion, 147th Infantry, and landed unopposed at Aola Bay on 4 November 1942 under Colonel W. B. Tuttle, after which command passed to Vandegrift. The claim locates the regiment by that 1st Battalion landing, the body Miller names. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

location_qualifier: Aola Bay area, last claimed location
source_locator: R2225: ch. IX, General Patch Takes Command, as already cited on C12786 and C12912
current_activity: leaving 1st Marine Division command when Patch took command ashore
notes: Inferred command change, same pattern as the 164th Infantry (C12821) and the 182nd Infantry (C12912). Miller, chapter IX, dates Patch's assumption of command of troops ashore to 9 December 1942, when the Americal Division headquarters took over from the 1st Marine Division. The 147th had landed at Aola Bay on 4 November while Vandegrift still commanded ashore. The location is the last claimed place (Aola), not a newly sourced 9 December movement. Confidence 0.5: inferred from that command change.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, Plans and Preparations; R2226: ch. IX, Final Period
current_activity: landing the Beaufort Bay expedition at Klerk's mission at 1315
notes: Miller, ch. XIV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that the 147th Infantry shore-to-shore expedition landed on the south coast at Beaufort Bay on 9 January 1943. Miller describes Captain Beach's force (I Company, a platoon of M, a platoon of the Antitank Company, and pioneer, medical, and communication troops) boarded two LCTs at Kukum on 7 January and reached Klerk's mission at 1315 on 9 January, then established beach defenses. Zimmerman confirms the passage was accomplished that day without incident. The claim locates the regiment by that named detachment. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: Vurai, on the trail north of Beaufort Bay
source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, Plans and Preparations
current_activity: reaching Vurai and establishing a block on the Kokumbona-Beaufort Bay trail
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: two days after the 9 January landing, the remainder of Beach's 147th Infantry expedition set out over the mountain trail and reached Vurai on 14 January 1943, established a base camp and outposts, and later moved the main camp to Tapananja on the upper Nueha. No Japanese used the trail. Vurai is not in the GeoNames Solomon Islands gazetteer used for these places, so the claim is pinned at Beaufort Bay, the sourced starting bay, with the inland village as a qualifier. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Zimmerman confirms a strong point near Tapinanja but does not give the 14 January date.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, The CAM Division
current_activity: leaving Koli Point and moving up to the Point Cruz area
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: by late afternoon of 19 January 1943 the Americal Reconnaissance Squadron had relieved the 147th Infantry at Koli Point, and the 147th moved up to the Point Cruz area. I Company remained on the Beaufort Bay trail. The claim locates the 1st and 3rd Battalions (less I Company) named in the CAM Division line. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, The CAM Division
current_activity: attacking in the CAM Division center and seizing Hill 95
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: on 22 January 1943 the 147th Infantry advanced in the center of the CAM Division attack and seized Hill 95; patrols met machine-gun fire in the ravine to the west. 3rd Battalion (plus C Company, less I Company) had moved into the front line between the 6th Marines and the 182nd on 20-21 January. I Company remained at Beaufort Bay. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: passing through west of the Nueha and reaching the Bonegi mouth on the beach
notes: Miller, ch. XV: the 147th Infantry passed through the lines west of the Nueha to attack about 0700 on 30 January 1943. On the beach, 1st Battalion advanced against light opposition to the mouth of the Bonegi, about 2,000 yards west of the Nueha; a patrol crossed about 1152 but withdrew when fire from the west bank hit the battalion. Inland, machine guns stopped 3rd Battalion 1,000 yards east of the Bonegi. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. The regiment was still under De Carre until 1 February.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: crossing the Bonegi and making contact south of Tassafaronga
notes: Miller, ch. XV: on 2 February 1943 1st Battalion, 147th Infantry, crossed the Bonegi at its mouth, and by 1710 the 1st and 3rd Battalions had made contact south of Tassafaronga. The crossing cost two killed and sixty-seven wounded. Zimmerman, ch. IX, writes that the drive carried American forces into Tassafaronga on 31 January; because that day does not match Miller's 2 February contact, confidence remains 0.5 (Miller only). Command of the western pursuit had passed to Sebree on 1 February.
